red_interpretation: This blueprint contains NO red marks (pixel-verified: 0 red pixels). Its construction feature is drawn instead as a band of fine gray strokes directly below the yoke seam: these represent gathering (shirring) — the Neapolitan gathered fullness where the back body is eased into the yoke. They must be rendered as real gathered-fabric ripples in white cloth, not as lines or texture. In sibling back blueprints (e.g. double-darts, which shows 2 red vertical lines), red marks dart stitch-seams or pleat folds; this option deliberately has none — the absence of red confirms zero darts and zero pleats.
geometry_summary: Rear view, long-sleeve dress shirt back, 209x243 px blueprint. Two-piece collar (band + turned collar) at top. A single straight horizontal yoke seam spans the full back width armhole-to-armhole at y=47-48; collar base at y=19, hem center at y=238, so yoke depth = 28 px vs 191 px lower panel (yoke ≈ 1/6.8 of the seam-to-hem length; ~13% of center-back length). Immediately below the yoke seam, a continuous full-width band of fine irregular vertical gathering strokes (roughly 35-45 drawn) with no gap at center; most ripples dissipate within ~20 px (≈5-7 cm real-world), a few longer strokes reaching ~45 px (~8-9 cm). Below the gathers the back is one completely clean panel: no darts, no pleats, no center-back seam; only gentle S-curve waist suppression at the side seams. Curved shirttail hem drawn as a double line: side-seam hem points at y=222, center-back dips to y=238 (16 px ≈ 5-6 cm drop, ~8% of lower-panel height). Sleeves hang at the sides with gauntlet plackets and buttoned barrel cuffs (standard, not the showcased feature).
